item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 132327
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
newly formed Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located several hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.8N 134.0W

ABOUT 1375 MI...2215 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 18.8 North, longitude 134.0 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h), and a 
west-northwestward to westward motion is expected during the next 
few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Some fluctuations in intensity remain possible 
for the rest of the day, followed by a gradual weakening trend after 
that.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Brown

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Sep 13 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 132037
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 AM HST Sun Sep 13 2026
 
Visible satellite imagery indicates that Norbert’s center has become 
exposed. The bulk of the convection is located on the south and east 
sides of the storm. Water vapor imagery shows that a good amount of 
dry air has penetrated into the core of the cyclone. The latest TAFB 
Dvorak fix estimated the intensity around 45 kt and the objective 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS are in the range of 32-39 kt. In 
addition, recent ASCAT pass shows that the strongest winds close to 
the center were around 37 kt. Therefore, the initial intensity has 
been lowered to 40 kt for this advisory.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be 290/11 kt. The storm is
expected to move west-northwestward to westward as it moves to the
south of a low- to mid-level subtropical ridge. The track guidance
continues to have good agreement on the general heading for this
storm. The current NHC track forecast has been nudged slightly to
north of the previous forecast track and remains close to the 
corrected multi-model consensus (HCCA) and the Google DeepMind 
(GDMI) ensemble mean.
 
More fluctuations in intensity are possible in the short term as 
Norbert remains in a marginal environment. The cyclone continues to 
contend with mid-level dry air intrusions and light west- 
southwesterly vertical wind shear.  After 12 h, the wind shear 
is expected to increase, which should result in a gradual weakening. 
Around 60 h, the simulated GFS and ECMWF satellite imagery shows 
that the cyclone should lose organized deep convection and it is 
therefore expected to become a post-tropical remnant low and then 
dissipate by around 72 h. The current NHC intensity forecast 
remains in line with the latest guidance including the HCCA and 
GDMI consensus guidance.

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026

...DEPRESSION COULD BECOME A TROPICAL STORM LATER TONIGHT OR 
EARLY MONDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.0N 118.3W
ABOUT 680 MI...1095 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 260 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 17.0 North, longitude 118.3
West.  The depression is moving toward the west near 10 mph (17 
km/h).  A slightly faster westward to west-southwestward motion is 
forecast during the couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some slight strengthening is expected overnight, and the 
depression is forecast to become a tropical storm by early Monday.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 140235
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
800 PM PDT Sun Sep 13 2026

The depression has not become better organized since earlier today. 
Visible satellite images show that the well-defined low-level 
center remains displaced and exposed to the northwest of the main 
area of deep convection.  Using measurements with the Dvorak shear 
pattern, the intensity of the cyclone is estimated to be below 
tropical storm strength.  Thus the current intensity estimate 
remains 30 kt, which is in agreement with earlier scatterometer 
observations.

Water vapor imagery shows that the system is currently being 
affected by moderate vertical wind shear and relatively dry 
mid-tropospheric air.  Global model guidance indicates that these 
marginal to unfavorable conditions are likely to persist for the 
next few days. Therefore, only slight short-term strengthening is 
called for and the system is expected to begin weakening in a day 
or so, with the cyclone degenerating into a remnant low in 96 hours 
or sooner.  This is consistent with simulated satellite imagery 
depicted by the ECMWF model run.  

The depression is moving a little south of due west with an 
initial motion of around 260/9 kt.  A mid-level ridge to the north 
of the system should keep the cyclone on a mainly westward track 
with a slightly increase in forward speed for the next 72-96 hours. 
The official track forecast is similar to, but not quite as fast 
as, the latest Google DeepMind and corrected model consensus, 
HCCA, guidance.
